name: AX30G analog input stage: Input Level -> +15 dB amp with pre-emphasis -> ADC full scale -> de-emphasis
input_level_notes: dB relative to the LIN captures (the campaign's reference Input Level setting). MAX (fully clockwise) is +14.0509 dB, measured as the small-signal gain difference between the MAX and LIN Bypass captures: +14.0498 dB mean with 0.0055 dB spread over 86 sweep windows below 7 kHz.

At 0.0 (LIN) the stage is transparent for every segment of the signal set: the shelf and its exact inverse cancel and nothing reaches the ceiling (the model's LIN Bypass null is -30.6/-30.5 dB with the stage on or off).
This is a real gain, not a trim: on the unit the Input Level pot is ahead of the +15 dB amplifier, so MAX really is 14 dB louder out as well as 14 dB closer to the ceiling.

notes: H(s) = (1 + s*tau_zero)/(1 + s*tau_pole), unity at DC: +0.58 dB at 1 kHz, +2.8 at 3 k, +5.2 at 5 k, +7.3 at 8 k, +8.1 at 10 k, +9.2 at 15 k, +9.6 at 19 k relative to 1 kHz, asymptote +10.93 dB.

Fitted to 25 sweep points (7.7-17.6 kHz, from how much earlier each frequency reaches the ceiling at a fixed level) and 9 harmonic points (3-19 kHz, from how far the clipped ramp's harmonics sit below the analytic hard-clip harmonics): 0.23 dB weighted rms. tests/input_stage_test.py measure reproduces it.

Service manual p. 21/33: the inverting +15 dB stage's input leg is R125 in parallel with (R129 + C107), which gives (1 + s(R125+R129)C107)/(1 + s*R129*C107). R129*C107 = 3.9k * 4700 pF = 18.33 us against the 18.17 us fitted here (0.9 %); the zero's 63.94 us wants R125+R129 = 13.6k where the schematic reads 10.7k, so either R125 is not 6.8k or C107 is not exactly 4700 pF.

Discretise with engine.render.shelf1_coeffs: a first-order least-squares fit to the analog magnitude over 20 Hz - 0.999*Nyquist, 0.21 dB max and 0.030 dB rms error. NOT a plain bilinear - the two corners cannot both be prewarped in one bilinear, and prewarping either one leaves the digital filter 2.2 dB high at 17 kHz at the device rate. The de-emphasis is the same filter with b and a swapped, which is its exact inverse, so below the ceiling the pair is transparent to floating-point rounding.

The ceiling is the converter's own full scale (+-1.0 in the DSP domain, the same clip engine/render.py's 18-bit _converter applies). headroom_dbfs is how far the input file's 0 dBFS sits BELOW it with Input Level at LIN, so the stage's gain is 10^((input_level_db - headroom_dbfs)/20).

+2.0605 dB comes from the measured 1 kHz clip point: a 1 kHz sine at MAX starts compressing at -12.574 dBFS in the file, MAX is +14.0509 dB, and the shelf is +0.5834 dB at 1 kHz at the device rate. So at LIN a full-scale 1 kHz sine is still 1.48 dB short of the ADC ceiling, which is why every LIN capture in the campaign is clean. An independent scan of headroom_dbfs against the clipped part of the MAX ramp peaks at 2.07 dB.

Hard clip, not a soft curve and not a delta-sigma grit burst: the fundamental-compression law measured on the MAX ramp follows the analytic hard-clip law to 0.019 dB rms over 18 dB of drive, while a tanh of any threshold is 0.80 dB rms off. The only departure is at the knee, where the measurement is 0.06 dB softer than the ideal.

offset_frac: a DC offset at the clipper as a fraction of full scale, added before the clip and removed after (equivalently, thresholds +1-d and -1-d). It is the only source of even harmonics. 0.027 puts H2 on the capture at the ramp's top (-46.5 dBFS); it then leaves H4 4 dB and H6 5 dB low, because the capture's even series falls about 3 dB per order and a single offset falls about 6. The ramp null is within 0.16 dB anywhere from 0.010 to 0.030.

oversample: clip at N times the device rate and band-limit back, i.e. treat the clip as analog ahead of the decimation filter. Measured 2026-09-16: N=2/4/8 leave the ramp null unchanged (-26.6 dB) and put the fold-back of the harmonics above Nyquist 8-14 dB BELOW the capture, where N=1 puts it within 3 dB. The unit's decimator therefore passes 21 kHz well enough to fold it back, and clipping on the sample grid is the closer model. Keep 1.
The manual's 'peak input level, full scale -1 dB'; LED15 is the SAA7366T's OVLD flag, after the pre-emphasis. In the model: light it when the clipper's input peak reaches 10^(-1/20) = 0.8913.

Every bracket of the 2026-09-13 Peak-by-frequency table is reproduced by this shelf, this ceiling and the -1 dB rule: predicted Peak thresholds in file dBFS are MAX 100 Hz -13.0, 1 k -13.6, 4 k -17.6, 10 k -21.7, 16 k -23.0; LIN 100 Hz +1.1, 1 k +0.5, 4 k -3.6, 10 k -7.6, 16 k -9.0. The observed brackets were MAX -12/-12/-12/below -20/below -20 and LIN never/0/-3/-6/-6.
